healthCheck.verifiedOn: the service record, re-read after the PATCH
healthCheck.whyNotHealthLive: /health/live reports only that the process is up. /health/ready additionally consults the database and, in the §268 candidate, the expected schema version — so it distinguishes 'running' from 'safe to serve'.
healthCheck.exercisedBy: the same-SHA restart; the service returned HTTP 200 ready on the first probe afterwards

If the migrations have not been applied, the health check fails and Render will not treat the deploy as live — which is the fail-closed ordering the runbook exists to enforce, now enforced by the platform rather than by a human remembering.

buildMetadata.defectBefore: backend/src/build-info.ts hardcodes buildTimestamp 2026-06-19T20:42:00Z. getBuildMetadata() resolved gitCommit from a chain of environment variables but read buildTimestamp from the literal alone, so /health/version reported a date four months older than the running build and would have done so for every future release.
buildMetadata.fix: buildTimestamp now resolves BUILD_TIMESTAMP -> RENDER_BUILD_TIMESTAMP -> VERCEL_DEPLOYMENT_CREATED_AT -> SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH -> the checked-in literal, and a new buildTimestampSourceStatus field reports which source answered — on the same footing as versionSourceStatus does for the commit.
buildMetadata.malformedInputRejected: a value that does not parse is rejected rather than echoed onto the health endpoint, and falls through to the next usable source
buildMetadata.epochAccepted: SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is normalised from Unix seconds to ISO-8601
buildMetadata.injectionMechanism: Dockerfile accepts a BUILD_TIMESTAMP build ARG, mirroring the existing GIT_COMMIT ARG; the release process sets it immediately before deploying
buildMetadata.optionChosen: the third of the three §270 permitted options — release-process injection rather than a stamping build step. build:render is bare tsc and Render supplies no build-time timestamp, and changing the build pipeline immediately before a first release is the riskier trade.
buildMetadata.whyForgettingItIsNowSafe: a missing injection yields buildTimestampSourceStatus BUILD_FALLBACK, which states on its face that the value is not a stamp. The silent-wrong-answer failure mode is gone; that visibility is the actual fix.
buildMetadata.gitCommitMechanism: UNCHANGED — still resolved from the platform commit variable first, reported as versionSourceStatus, and release:verify-sha still refuses a BUILD_FALLBACK answer
buildMetadata.test: npm run test:270-build-metadata — 12 checks, PASS, covering precedence, epoch normalisation, fallback identification, malformed-input rejection and fall-through, and unchanged commit resolution

regressionIntroducedAndFixed.whatHappened: Two §269/§270 documentation edits inside executable code broke checks that depend on it, and both were caught by running the checks rather than by review.

one.defect: naming the provider credential variable and the platform commit variable as string literals in scripts/beta-readiness.ts caused the script registry to classify it PROVIDER_CALLING and LIVE_ENVIRONMENT. It calls no provider and contacts nothing live.
one.whyItMatters: the classifier's own docblock warns that a registry whose loudest warnings sit on its safety tooling is one people learn to ignore
one.fix: reworded to describe the variables without naming them; beta-readiness is plain READ_ONLY again and PROVIDER_CALLING returned to its 63 baseline

two.defect: the §270 runbook preamble quoted the later step titles DEPLOY THE EXACT SHA and VERIFY THE RUNNING SHA above the migration sections. beta:readiness asserts step ordering by FIRST occurrence, so it reported that DEPLOY preceded MIGRATE — failing the two checks that guard the release's core safety property.
two.fix: the preamble now refers to 'step 6 below' and 'step 7 below' without quoting the titles. The check was not weakened. Ordering re-verified as strictly monotonic across all eight steps.
